[Purpose and High-Level Scope of Services]
The purpose of this Business Requirements Document (BRD) is to capture the detailed requirements aligning with the scope, and deliverables for the transition and ongoing management of Mailroom and Data Capture Operations for . As part of the engagement, Smart Data Solutions (SDS) will assume responsibility for the intake, processing, digitization, and secure transmission of incoming mail and related documents. This transition aims to improve operational efficiency, ensure regulatory compliance, and enhance data accuracy through advanced technologies and workflow automation.
section_title: Purpose and High-Level Scope of Services

[Scope]
A successful implementation depends on clear, shared understanding, down to the lowest level of operational detail. To eliminate assumptions and ensure both parties are fully aligned, we prioritize documenting every element of scope with precision. The more specific we are upfront, the smoother the implementation will run.

[Critical Deliverables to Ensure a Strong Start]
To accelerate progress and reduce rework, the following deliverables are essential early in the implementation process. These items allow SDS to begin configuration, align automation efforts, and lay the groundwork for testing and validation. Prompt delivery and review of these materials will ensure a smoother implementation and help both teams hit the ground running:
Sample Files: One week’s worth of each document type (e.g., claims, EOBs, correspondence)
Process Documentation: Existing workflows, routing logic, intake handling guides, and decision points
Eligibility & Provider Files: Current format/layout and sample data
PO Box/Fax/SFTP Intake Setup: Number or directory assignment, and access credentials
Key Contacts: Client SMEs for intake, business rules, IT, and testing support
These deliverables serve as the foundation for effective analysis, configuration, and documentation throughout the project.
section_title: Critical Deliverables to Ensure a Strong Start

text:
[Input Channels]
Our platform is designed to support a wide range of intake channels to meet clients where they are in their digital transformation journey. These may include physical mail via PO boxes, secure file transfer (SFTP), fax, API integrations, web uploads, client-scanned solutions, and forwarded email inboxes.
The specific input channels activated for this implementation will be captured in detail to ensure proper configuration, routing, and operational readiness in alignment with the Statement of Work (SOW).

[Client Performed Scanning Integration]
In this model, the ABC Corporation is responsible for scanning source documents and serving as their own mailroom. SDS will configure the necessary functionality to enable secure, direct integration between the ABC Corporation’s scanning equipment and SDS’ QuickClaim platform. Upon receipt, SDS will perform all downstream data capture and processing activities as defined within this BRD.
Image Submission Standards
To ensure successful ingestion and high-quality data capture, all scanned images submitted to SDS must meet the following minimum requirements:
Resolution: 300 DPI
File Format: Bilevel CCITT Group 4 TIFF
Form Processing: Red dropout enabled for CMS-1500 and UB-04 claim forms
Image Quality: No skewing, cropping, or shadowing; legible and suitable for OCR/data extraction
Special Attachments: Grayscale or color allowed only for designated attachment types (e.g., EOBs with color-coded notes)
Scanning Hardware Requirements
If SDS is responsible for configuring or supporting a scanning setup within the ABC Corporation’s facility, scanning must occur on SDS-approved equipment. Supported models include:
Canon DR-G2090
Canon DR-G2110
Canon DR-G2140
Alternative models must be pre-approved by SDS to ensure compatibility with ingestion workflows and image quality standards.
Pre-Scan Document Preparation & Indexing Expectations
To ensure efficiency in processing and proper document classification, SDS requires clarity on the ABC Corporation’s role in pre-scan preparation. The following areas must be defined for this implementation: document separation, document type identification, sorting requirements,
Document Separation: Will the ABC Corporation separate documents by type prior to scanning (e.g., claim forms, appeals, correspondence)?
Document Type Identification: Will the ABC Corporation insert barcodes, cover sheets, or use folder structures to denote document types?
Sorting Requirements: Will documents be sorted by line of business, PO box, or submission type?
For this implementation, the requirements are as follows:
[Insert specifics and responsibilities, equipment setup, barcode usage, file packaging rules, etc.]

[Out of Scope (OOS) Mail]
Documents scanned in to SDS that are not part of the agreed upon scope will not be processed as part of the standard workflow; instead, they will be handled according to the ABC Corporation’s specified preference. ABC Corporations may choose to have OOS mail returned via ZIP file with rejected images at an agreed upon interval. The handling of OOS mail will be captured in the Export File Format section: [1.3.11.2].
For this implementation, OOS mail is defined as:
Any scanned document without a standard CMS1500 or ADA Dental form present, which includes, but is not limited to, UB04s, medical records without claims attached, and non-standard member submit claim forms.

[SFTP Intake]
SDS supports a secure, automated intake of ABC Corporation-submitted documents via Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP). This method allows for high-volume, encrypted file transfers from the ABC Corporation’s environment directly into SDS’ processing pipeline. Files are picked up at defined intervals and routed according to predefined business rules, enabling efficient, near real-time ingestion without manual intervention. As with other intake channels, all ABC Corporation-specific requirements for folder structure, file naming conventions, and delivery expectations must be clearly documented within this BRD to ensure successful and traceable processing.

[Connectivity]
SDS supports flexible SFTP configurations, including pull/push or push/push connectivity. We recommend a push/push model for enhanced control, reliability, and monitoring. SDS will establish the connection and provide a configuration form to be completed by the ABC Corporation, which captures connectivity preferences, IP whitelisting, folder structures, and authorization details.
For this implementation, the connection method is as follows:
PUSH / PULL
The SFTP account will be hosted by SDS with connectivity maintained in a “PUSH / PULL” configuration. Under this configuration, the ABC Corporation will upload inbound files to the inbound folders on the SDS-hosted SFTP account, while SDS delivers outbound files to the outbound folders on the same SDS-hosted SFTP account. PGP encryption will not be used on exchanged files.

[Intake Folder Structure]
SDS supports both flat and tiered folder structures based on ABC Corporation preferences. Common configurations include separate folders by document type, line of business, or priority level. ABC Corporations must identify the expected folder layout, and SDS will map processing logic accordingly.
For this implementation, the intake folder structure on the SDS-hosted SFTP will be configured as follows:

Any additional intake files identified during the configuration process will have an additional folder created using the naming convention below. The ABC Corporation shall not create any additional folders outside the agreed-upon structure. Files uploaded to unauthorized locations may be excluded from processing.

Test: /in/test/[FILE DESCRIPTION]/

[File Naming Convention]
SDS requires all incoming files to follow a consistent and clearly defined naming convention to ensure accurate processing, tracking, and error prevention. File names should be unique, structured, and easily traceable. SDS strongly recommends including a date and timestamp (formatted as YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS) along with other relevant identifiers such as ABC Corporation name, document type, or batch ID. This helps avoid processing delays, misrouting, and downstream reconciliation issues.
Files that are improperly formatted or contain duplicate file names within the processing window will be automatically rejected to prevent reprocessing, data integrity issues, or unintended overwrites. Rejected files will be flagged through exception monitoring and reported to the ABC Corporation for correction and resubmission. Exception handling rules should be documented in the Exception Monitoring section of this BRD.
For this implementation, the required file naming conventions are:
Member Eligibility:
ABC Corporation_SDS_<Line of Business>_<DateTimeStamp>.dat

This will either be COMMERCIAL or MEDICAID

Acknowledgements will be picked up from the /in/EDI/999 folder regardless of the naming convention. The only requirement is that the file extension is ‘.999’.

[File Size Limitations]
To ensure efficient file transfer, system performance, and timely processing, SDS recommends limiting individual file sizes to an optimal threshold. Extremely large files can cause delays in intake, increase the risk of transfer failure, and negatively impact downstream processing workflows. While SDS can accommodate large file sizes, when necessary, expectations should be clearly defined to avoid interruptions.
For this implementation, the maximum supported file size is: 2GB

[Delivery Type]
SDS supports both batch-based and near real-time delivery models via SFTP. SDS polls the SFTP directory every 20 minutes to check for newly submitted files, enabling frequent intake without manual triggers. ABC Corporations have full control over when and how often they post files to SFTP, but critical files, such as member eligibility and provider files, require clearly defined delivery expectations. For these file types, SDS relies on timely and complete delivery to maintain downstream integrity and automation. ABC Corporations should establish thresholds and fallback rules to manage exceptions (e.g., missing or abnormally small files). Exception handling rules, such as triggering alerts or continuing to use the prior day's file, should be documented in the Exception Monitoring section of this BRD.
For this implementation, the expected delivery and schedule are:

[Exception Monitoring]
SDS offers robust exception monitoring to identify and proactively alert ABC Corporations to issues that may disrupt processing, data integrity, or expected timelines. ABC Corporations may define custom rules and thresholds for critical files, such as eligibility or provider data, including scenarios where files are not received by a defined time (e.g., membership file not received by 8:00 AM ET), file record counts decrease unexpectedly (e.g., >80% reduction), or acknowledgments (e.g., 999, 277) are not returned within a specified window (e.g., 48 hours). When exceptions are triggered, SDS can send email notifications to ABC Corporation-defined distribution lists to ensure prompt awareness and resolution.
In addition to email notifications, key alerts are prominently displayed on the homepage of the SDS QuickClaim portal, making exception status visible to all authorized users. This ensures broad visibility beyond just the recipients of the notifications. ABC Corporations are responsible for defining the exception rules and providing distribution lists for critical alerts. Furthermore, SDS provides a set of standard notifications available to all ABC Corporations, which can be enabled or disabled by a ABC Corporation administrator within the Access Management section of the portal via simple checkboxes.
For this implementation, the following exception monitoring rules and notification preferences will apply:

The alert email configuration is:

Subject Line: Alert emails will be configured so that the subject line states the exception type and time of email generation (i.e. Subject Line: “Critical File Not Received yyyy-MM-dd").
Email Body: The body of the email will be dependent on the triggered exception type:
Critical File Not Received: Body of email will contain most recent file name and when it was loaded.
Extract Volume Drop: Body of email will contain % discrepancy, previous file’s volume, and the comparative volume received.
Corrupt Extract File: Body of email will contain the file name and time of receipt.
Missing Acknowledgement: Body of email will contain claim files containing claims that have not received acknowledgement for >72 hours.
No Scanned Volume: Body of email will contain alert that SDS has not received volume for the agreed upon threshold time.
Aging File: Body of email will contain name of files that are pending in SDS’ outbound SFTP folders that have not been removed by ABC Corporation.

[Document Control Number (DCN) Assignment, Formatting, and Placement]
SDS assigns a unique Document Control Number (DCN) to each inbound document to enable tracking, processing, and auditability throughout the document lifecycle. DCNs are generated based on a ABC Corporation-specific format that may include a combination of date, document type, intake channel, ABC Corporation ID, batch number, or other identifiers. Once defined, DCNs will be embedded into all applicable metadata and output files and may also be used in reconciliation and reporting processes. By default, the DCN will be placed in the top right corner of all document images; if an alternate placement is required, it must be explicitly specified below.
For this implementation, the DCN will be configured as follows:
<Form Type (1-byte)> <Scanner Identifier (1-byte)> <Julian Date (5-byte)> <3 - Batch Counter (3-byte)> <Document Counter (3-byte)>

[Document Splitting]
ABC Corporation performs document splitting as part of the mailroom preprocessing and preparation of incoming batches. An approved document separator will be inserted between each document within a batch so that upon scanning, SDS is able to determine a clear beginning and end to each document.
If a set of documents require a “global” attachment (for example if an envelope contains multiple documents that require envelope scanning), a copy of the “global” attachment must be appended to each document by creating multiple copies or use of an approved Global Attachment Separator.

[Document Identification]
ABC Corporation performs document identification as part of the mailroom preprocessing and preparation of incoming batches. The document type (CMS1500 or Dental ADA), as well as any additional batch traits (EOBs attached, Xray sticker attached, Global attachment included, etc) should be clearly marked on a batch coversheet and input into the scanner at time of scanning. All documents within a batch must have the same document type and document trait(s).

[Document Types]
As part of the configuration process, ABC Corporations must define the full set of document types that SDS will receive and process. From the pre-processing document types, the resulting post-processing document types below may be achieved:

[Data Capture]
SDS provides flexible, high-accuracy data capture services that extract structured data elements from a wide range of document types. Our platform supports both automated and manual data entry workflows, configured to meet each client’s specific business and regulatory requirements. Captured fields are used to support downstream processing, validation, routing, and integration with client systems.
Data capture configurations are defined at the document type level and are organized into the following categories. For this implementation, the following capture configurations are in scope:
Standard Claims: CMS-1500 and ADA Dental forms with predefined field mapping and validation.
X-Ray Sticker ID Capture: Documents that are scanned in with ‘Xray Sticker’ will be routed to supplemental capture for capture and mapping of sticker identifier.
Data capture configurations that are not in scope for this implementation include:
Standard Claims: UB04 forms with predefined field mapping and validation.
Non-Standard Claims: Includes member-submitted forms, pharmacy receipts, and other custom formats requiring ABC Corporation-specific rules.
Explanation of Benefits (EOBs): Capture of payer adjudication data, including allowed amounts, adjustments, and payment references.
Correspondence: Structured capture of key fields such as Member ID, Claim Number, Appeal Type, and Date of Service, supporting queueing and resolution workflows.
Each document type will have its own defined index fields, validation logic, and exception handling criteria as detailed in the subsections that follow.

[CMS1500 and ADA Dental Claim Forms]
SDS supports automated data capture from standard claim forms, including CMS-1500 and ADA Dental Claim Forms. These forms are processed using a combination of optical character recognition (OCR), business rules, and human validation to ensure high accuracy and compliance with payer and regulatory requirements. Data is extracted at the field level (e.g., Member ID, Provider NPI, Tooth Number, CDT Codes, Claim Amount, Date of Service), with validation logic configured to align with SNIP standards, payer-specific rules, and ABC Corporation-defined business needs.
section_title: CMS1500 and ADA Dental Claim Forms

text:
[Matching File Type]
SDS relies on industry-standard eligibility files or comma-delimited file with required data elements to perform member validation, with the HIPAA-compliant ANSI X12 834 format serving as the primary file type. The membership file provides essential member-level data used during the matching process to verify identity and eligibility based on captured document information.
The membership file must include core elements such as Member ID, Subscriber ID, First Name, Last Name, Date of Birth, and Coverage Effective Dates. These fields are used to validate and associate incoming documents with an active member record, supporting both operational accuracy and compliance.
While SDS adheres to standard 834 / member file processing logic, ABC Corporation-specific nuances, such as unique identifiers, can be configured.
For this implementation, the Membership File will contain the following information:

[Matching File Frequency & Retention]
SDS supports a variety of eligibility file delivery cadences, including full file transmissions and change-only files. These files are used to drive accurate member matching, coverage validation, and downstream routing logic within the SDS platform.
While ABC Corporations may vary in how they structure and transmit eligibility data, the frequency and type of file have a significant impact on matching accuracy, claim rejections, and the ability to process retroactive updates. Additionally, SDS must understand how long terminated members should remain available to support appeals, retro claims, and historical validation. SDS recommends ABC Corporations provide daily full eligibility files to ensure consistent and accurate member matching across all intake channels. Additionally, we recommend retaining termination records for 18–24 months to support retroactive processing, adjustments, audits, and other downstream activities.
However, longer retention periods may be required based on regulatory filing limits or specific business needs—for example, Medicaid programs often require extended data availability beyond standard retention windows.
For this implementation, the following frequency and retention rules will apply:
Membership File: Full extract to be sent daily; [XX] months of termination records

[Matching Logic and Exception Processing]
During intake, SDS applies member matching logic to associate incoming documents with eligibility records using key fields such as Member ID, Name, Date of Birth, and other configurable identifiers. This logic is defined in a standard mapping document, which serves as the baseline for all implementations.
For this implementation, the matching logic and rules that will apply are located in [Attachment].
Exception handling occurs when documents cannot be matched through automated logic. SDS offers flexible options for managing these scenarios:
Manual Matching Queue: Unmatched records can be routed to a manual matching queue that the ABC Corporation can access and manage.
Note: This is especially critical if daily full files are not provided, as fallouts are more likely.
Recommended Practice: SDS recommends enabling the manual matching queue during the initial warranty period of all implementations. This ensures early detection and resolution of logic or data discrepancies and validates that matching processes are performing as expected.
Post-Validation Options:
Unmatched document scan be:
Routed to the manual matching queue (continuation of the process)
Routed through the ABC Corporation’s reject processes
Exported back to the ABC Corporation for additional investigation or actions (e.g., leaving blank or applying a default)
Trigger Scope:
Matching logic can be applied across all document documents, or configured to target a specific subset – e.g.,
Included: Claim forms, appeals, and reconsiderations
Excluded: Enrollment packets, provider correspondence, and general inquiries
For this implementation, the following exception handling rules will apply:

[Rejections]
As part of our data capture and validation processes, certain submissions may be rejected when required information is missing, invalid, or fails to meet defined business rules. Rejections are categorized, tracked, and either returned to the sender or routed to the ABC Corporation for further action. The goal is to ensure data integrity while supporting timely resolution and clear communication.
Rejections may occur during intake, data validation (against internal or ABC Corporation-provided code sets or business rules), or during matching logic. Standard rejection handling includes classification, manual review, optional letter generation, and export or routing to the appropriate party.

[Rejection Logic and Rejection Reason Codes]
SDS maintains a set of standard rejection reason codes aligned with our core data capture and validation processes. These are based on industry-standard code sets, internal validation rules, and system checks against required claim fields. Common examples include:
Missing or invalid diagnosis or procedure codes
Invalid or missing NPI
Missing Explanation of Benefits (EOB)
Mismatch with provider or member records
Unreadable or corrupted image
In addition to SDS’s standard rules, ABC Corporation-specific rejection logic may be required based on claim type, form version, or business rules.
For this implementation, the defined rejection reason codes and associated field-level validations are included in [Attachment]
section_title: Rejection Logic and Rejection Reason Codes

text:
[Rejection Review Processes]
For any document that triggers a reject condition, SDS will first route the document to an internal reject queue for review and validation. This allows SDS to confirm whether the issue was due to a data capture error (e.g., manual entry issue, OCR misread) or a valid submission error.
If the issue is internal: SDS will correct the error and reprocess the document.
If the reject is valid: The document will be routed to the ABC Corporation-owned pended reject queue for further action.
The pended reject queue provides the ABC Corporation with full visibility of the rejected document, including:
Original document image
All captured data
Reject reason(s)
Within the pended reject queue, the ABC Corporation has the following options:
Verify the reject: Confirm the reject is valid and allow it to follow the agreed-upon downstream process. Possible downstream process selections are:
Rejection Letter to Provider
If the provider’s address information is complete, this will release the document to send the reject letter.
If the provider’s address is incomplete, the user will be prompted to complete the address. Once completed, the letter will be queued for submission.
If the address cannot be completed, “Send Reject Letter to Provider” action will not be able to be completed.
View Reject Letter
Remove From Queue
Challenge the reject: If ABC Corporation does not agree with the reject (e.g., reject does not follow expected logic, reject is triggered by erroneous data capture, etc), un-pend document from reject queue and allow it to follow the agreed-upon downstream process.
Un-pend:
Remove document from pended reject queue and route it back to SDS to correct captured value.
Note: The “un-pend” action is intended for erroneous data capture. If the reject is being disputed due to the incorrect logic application of a reject rule, user should reach out to support at ABC Corporation.support@sdata.us.
Rescan:
Edit Captured Information: If user would like to correct or supplement the captured data, particularly for member-submitted documents or exception processes where missing or replacement data can be populated.
Edit CMS1500 and Edit Dental:
After saving the changes in the document editor, document will revalidate against rejection scenarios. If document passes validation, document will route through non-rejected downstream processes.
Note: This functionality is also accessible in the Document Summary view, via “Edit CMS1500”/”Edit Dental”
SDS recommends maintaining this review queue throughout the warranty period to ensure all reject logic, document handling, and downstream processes are working as expected. Some ABC Corporations choose to retain this queue beyond warranty, either for specific high impact reject reasons or as an ongoing quality checkpoint.

[Rejection Letters]
SDS’ standard offering includes the generation and mailing of rejection letters for applicable provider-submitted claim forms. These letters are required when the submission includes incomplete or invalid information and cannot be processed without further clarification.
Rejection letters are created using a ABC Corporation-branded template, and SDS inserts the applicable reject reason(s) along with required claim details, such as:
Billing provider name and address (required for letter generation)
Member ID
Date(s) of Service
Total charges
Reference or control number (if applicable)
Letters are printed and mailed through our print and fulfillment partner. A sample copy of each letter is stored in our system and can be made available to the ABC Corporation alongside the original document image for audit or downstream system integration.
Note: Reject letters are typically generated only for provider-submitted claim forms, as they require the billing provider’s name and address for proper delivery. For any claim types with incomplete or missing information where a letter cannot be generated, an alternate resolution or routing process must be defined.

[Reject Letter Template]
ABC Corporations must provide one or more branded reject letter templates for use in production. If multiple templates are provided, logic must be clearly defined to determine when each should be used (e.g., use Template A for LOB A, Template B for commercial claims, etc.). SDS will populate the required fields based on available data captured during intake and validation.
If a required field (e.g., Member ID) is missing or illegible, SDS will follow ABC Corporation-approved conventions such as inserting “Unavailable” or leaving the field blank, depending on documented instructions.
For this implementation, the applicable template(s) and logic are included in [Attachment].

[ABC Corporation Workflows]
The SDS platform is a configurable workflow tool that supports customized process flows tailored to each ABC Corporation’s operational needs. These workflows allow for intelligent routing, manual intervention, and exception handling based on document type, data completeness, and ABC Corporation-specific business rules.
ABC Corporations may choose to route certain document types or scenarios to internal queues for manual review, correction, or approval. These workflows operate similarly to the member matching and provider matching review queues described earlier in this document.

Capstone Project Scoping Document

[Project Title:]
Student Capstone Project – Documentation Intelligence for Client Workflows

[Project Duration:]
10 Weeks (Approx. 40 hours/week, ~400 total hours)

[Project Type:]
Student Capstone Project – Applied AI & Documentation Engineering

[1. Project Overview]
Smart Data Solutions (SDS) seeks to automatically generate accurate, consumable documentation of client implementations by leveraging existing artifacts stored in SharePoint. Rather than manually standardizing or rewriting documentation, this capstone focuses on building an AI-assisted approach to discover, summarize, and synthesize client workflows and current-state configurations from SharePoint content. The student team will design and prototype a pipeline that ingests relevant artifacts (e.g., BRDs, plans, diagrams, status notes) and produces clear client summaries, workflow overviews, and ‘known gaps’ reports that can be used by Implementation, PM, Engineering, and Client stakeholders.

[2. Problem Statement]
Client documentation is fragmented across SharePoint and varies widely in structure and quality. As a result, new team members and stakeholders struggle to quickly understand a client’s current state, workflow nuances, and evidence of required artifacts. Prior attempts to standardize documentation or adopt third-party tools ran into security/process hurdles and did not yield durable change. SDS needs a scalable, low-friction way to generate and maintain living documentation—grounded in the artifacts teams already produce—without requiring access to production code

[Primary Objectives]
Design an AI-assisted documentation pipeline that ingests SharePoint artifacts and outputs client summaries and workflow narratives.
Produce clear, plain-language documentation usable by PMs, engineers, and clients (where appropriate).
Identify gaps and inconsistencies in available documentation; generate "what's missing" reports for audit readiness.
Establish prompts, templates, and evaluation criteria to measure documentation accuracy, usefulness, and effort saved.

[In Scope]
SharePoint-based content discovery and ingestion (e.g., BRDs, requirements, plans, diagrams, status notes, meeting summaries).
LLM-driven summarization and synthesis into standardized outputs: client overview, workflow map narrative, risks/assumptions/decisions (RAD), and evidence checklist.
Creation of reusable prompt sets, document templates, and a lightweight evaluation framework for accuracy and clarity.
Pilot on 1–2 representative clients’ SharePoint folders (redacted/synthetic where required).

[Out of Scope]
Direct analysis of production source code or full repository access.
Organization-wide SharePoint restructuring or enterprise governance overhaul.

[5. Access Requirements]
Systems / Tools
Shared collaboration space (SharePoint) for project materials, prompts, and outputs. (Implementation and Delivery SharePoint)
Read-only access to selected client folders or provision of exported/redacted documents representative of real projects.
Data
Implementation documentation and collateral.
Screenshots/PDFs of merge requests, client set-ups in QC, testcases (where applicable), etc.

[7. Key Deliverables]
•Client Overview Packet: 1–2 page summary per pilot client (scope, integrations, workflows, key decisions, open risks).
Workflow Narrative: Plain-language description of end-to-end processes with references back to source documents.
Evidence Presence Report: What artifacts exist, where they live, and what’s missing (to support audits/readiness).
Prompt & Template Library: Reusable prompts, output templates, and guidance for future teams.
Evaluation Framework: Accuracy, completeness, time-to-understand metrics; usability feedback from SMEs.
Final Presentation & Demo: Executive-ready summary, live demo/walkthrough, and recommendations for scaling.

[8. Success Criteria]
Summaries enable a new PM or engineer to understand a pilot client’s current state within 30–60 minutes.
Outputs accurately reflect the reality captured in SharePoint (validated by SMEs) and clearly call out gaps/assumptions.
Reusable prompts/templates are documented and can be applied to additional clients with minimal rework.
Security posture respected (no PHI; no code access); content retention follows SDS guidance.
